Topic.label: Figures with Line Symmetry and Reflection Symmetry Between Two Figures

Question: Which statement about two figures being reflections of each other across a line is correct?

Choices.A: Two congruent figures must be reflections of each other across a line.
Choices.B: Two figures that are reflections of each other must have a common point.
Choices.C: If folding a figure along a line makes its two sides coincide, these two figures are said to be reflections of each other.
Choices.D: Two figures that are reflections of each other must be congruent.

Solution: Two figures that are reflections of each other coincide completely when folded along the axis of reflection, so they must be congruent. However, congruent figures are not necessarily reflections of each other and do not necessarily have a common point.
